summary: All secure verbal occurrences fit I.1 hängen. Execution, threatened hanging and public suspension after decapitation (24/243) are contextual functions of the same suspension event.
German hängen lassen and liess aufhängen can express delegated execution while Turoyo remains stem I. No separate causative stem or sense is inferred.
Object suffixes, overt patients and fronted patients recur. Infinitiv šnoqo in qəm šnoqo wi has the speaker as prospective patient without Detransitive morphology.
Plural Preterit šnəqqe reflects q+l assimilation, not a new root. Variation šunq-/šənq- belongs to Infectum vocalism pending dialect checks.
Jan adds a Detransitive execution predicate and active Preterit-wa and Infectum-wa, absent after round 1. Hanging remains the single active sense.
Šniqi contrasts with agent-indexed šnəqwolən/šnəqwole/šnəqwolle. bu amrayḏe at Jan 3.1/18 names the authority whose orders were followed; it does not establish a normal Detransitive agent phrase.
Repetitions at Jan 1.29/1341–1343 are grouped into short examples. The source distinguishes report from eyewitness knowledge: Hawxa šaməʕina, lə ḥzelan.
Parenthetical šnoqo yo explains the legal loan ʕədam. This metalinguistic equivalence does not show that šnq covers every form of execution.
Active Preterit and Infectum have five examples each after round 1; routine historical reports need no further additions.
Is Hors 3/30 šanq an Arabic-pattern loan noun distinct from productive Infinitiv šnoqo? Excluded from the Infinitiv additions until clarified.

Check source šniqənne at 27/54 versus inherited šnəqənne; preserve both spellings pending edition verification.
Confirm singular šniq with šawʕo at Jan 1.22/1141 against plural šniqi at Jan 1.4/71; preserve recorded agreement.
